question:
A 64-year-old male reports persistent ulnar-sided pain in his right wrist and mild, constant tingling in the
fourth and fifth fingers following a golf-related wrist injury six months ago. While conservative treatment
has improved overall pain and function, he continues to experience difficulty with his golf performance.
Which diagnostic test should be obtained first to assist in confirming the diagnosis? Answer Choices:
(A) EMG study of the affected extremity (B) CT scan of the wrist (C) Arthrography of the wrist (D) Bone
scintigraphy of the wrist (E) Nerve conduction study of the ulnar nerve (F) Carpal tunnel view
radiograph (G) Plain radiograph of the cervical spine (H) Ultrasound of the wrist (I) Contrast enhanced
magnetic resonance angiogram (J) MRI of the cervical spine
 A. Arthrography of the wrist
B. Bone scintigraphy of the wrist
C. MRI of the cervical spine
D. Plain radiograph of the cervical spine
E. Nerve conduction study of the ulnar nerve
F. EMG study of the affected extremity
G. CT scan of the wrist
H. Contrast enhanced magnetic resonance angiogram
I. Ultrasound of the wrist
J. Carpal tunnel view radiograph
